data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.title: off
sections.question: off
sections.summary: away from a surface or place; no longer attached or connected to something

senses.definition: away from a surface or place; no longer attached or connected to something
examples: She takes off her coat when she gets home.
He jumps off the wall and lands on the ground.

answers.answer: She takes off her coat when she gets home.
She takes off her coat and it goes onto her body.
He offs his shoes before entering the house.
An off is a type of building where people work.

sections.title: on
sections.question: on
sections.summary: touching or supported by the surface of something

senses.definition: touching or supported by the surface of something
examples: She puts her book on the table.
He sits on the chair and reads his newspaper.

answers.answer: She puts her book on the table.
She sits on the sky and watches the clouds below her.
He ons his shoes before going to bed at night.
An on is something you eat for breakfast with eggs and toast.

sections.title: out
sections.question: out
sections.summary: away from the inside of a place; outside

senses.definition: away from the inside of a place; outside
examples: She takes the books out of her bag.
He goes out to buy some food from the store.

answers.answer: She takes the books out of her bag.
He goes out of the house and stays inside all day.
She outs her homework before going to school in the morning.
An out is a type of sport played in a big stadium.

sections.title: over
sections.question: over
sections.summary: above or higher than something; across the top of something

senses.definition: above or higher than something; directly covering or across something
examples: She hangs a picture over the fireplace.
He jumps over the small fence in the garden.

answers.answer: She hangs a picture over the fireplace.
He digs a hole over the ground to plant some seeds in it.
She overs her homework before going to sleep at night.
An over is a type of food you eat at a restaurant for dinner.

sections.title: to
sections.question: to
sections.summary: used to show movement in the direction of a place or person

senses.definition: used to show movement in the direction of a place or person
examples: She walks to school every morning.
He gives the book to his friend.

answers.answer: She walks to school every morning.
He travels to his home to leave it and go somewhere else.
She tos her homework before going to bed each night.
A to is a type of animal that lives in the ocean.

sections.title: under
sections.question: under
sections.summary: in or to a position that is below or beneath something

senses.definition: in or to a position that is below or beneath something
examples: She hides the present under her bed.
He finds his shoe under the sofa.

answers.answer: She hides the present under her bed.
He puts the picture under the wall to hang it high up.
She unders her coat before going outside in winter.
An under is a type of colour you can see in a rainbow.

sections.title: up
sections.question: up
sections.summary: towards a higher position or place; in an upward direction

senses.definition: towards a higher position or place; in an upward direction
examples: She climbs up the ladder to paint the ceiling.
He walks up the hill to enjoy the view.

answers.answer: She climbs up the ladder to paint the ceiling.
He walks up the hill and goes down to the top of it.
She ups her shoes before going to school each morning.
An up is a type of fruit that grows on trees in summer.

sections.title: with
sections.question: with
sections.summary: accompanied by someone; having or using something

senses.definition: accompanied by someone; having or using something
examples: She goes to the park with her friends.
He drinks his tea with a little milk.

answers.answer: She goes to the park with her friends.
He goes to the park with alone and meets nobody there.
She withs her homework before going to bed at night.
A with is a type of building in the middle of a busy city.
